comment: Grundy's game starts with a single heap of n tokens. A legal move consists of dividing a heap into two unequal parts. Since heaps of size 1 or 2 cannot be so divided, once the position has no heaps larger than 2, there are no legal moves, and according to the usual convention in such games, the first player who cannot move loses.
Note that Grundy's game is not an "octal game", because that formalism is not rich enough to capture the "unequal" splitting rule. (End)
